chase_cards.name: Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because the Hokushin'etsu print combines one of Pokémon's most mythic early creatures with a mountain-region Stadium. Mew makes the regional prize feel secretive rather than loud.

key_artists.name: "Big Mama" Tagawa and CR CG gangs
key_artists.why: This credit matters because Tagawa and CR CG gangs pull the card toward the early Creatures CG workshop: Stadium cards, 3D modeling, trainer objects, and the built world around Pokémon rather than only the Pokémon themselves.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Hokushin'etsu World Challenge Summer participation-prize source group as one row containing Lucky Stadium at source index 172.

Bulbapedia says Lucky Stadium was first awarded to participants of the Japanese World Challenge Summer tournaments held between July and August 2000, with eight variations printed, each one exclusive to a region of Japan.
Bulbapedia lists the Hokushin'etsu print, featuring Mew, as available at the Niigata City Industrial Promotion Center, Niigata on July 26, 2000.

PokeBoon identifies Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushinetsu] as a World Challenge Summer participation prize and gives the Mew/Hokushinetsu identity, while showing a May 14, 2000 distribution date that this dossier treats as a secondary-source date conflict against Bulbapedia's July 26 Summer event listing.
Bulbapedia's Lucky Stadium gallery credits the Hokushin'etsu region print to "Big Mama" Tagawa and CR CG gangs.
PokeBoon also credits Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushinetsu] to Big Mama Tagawa and CR CG gangs.

Bulbapedia says Yoshiyuki Tagawa, credited on cards as "Big Mama" Tagawa, worked as a graphic designer at Creatures, Inc., worked on 3D Pokémon models, illustrated Pokémon TCG cards, and has credits on Pokémon Stadium, Hey You, Pikachu!, Pokémon Snap, Pokémon Stadium 2, Pokémon Colosseum, and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness.
Bulbapedia describes CR CG gangs as a group of artists making Pokémon TCG illustrations, mostly Neo-era Trainer and Unown cards, and notes they were credited in Meowth's Party.
Bulbapedia says all World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium prints feature regional landmarks; the Hokushin'etsu print features several mountains of the Japanese Alps.

Bulbapedia separates the regional World Challenge Summer prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny English print, Intro Pack Neo print, and Pokemon Center New York print, each of which has different artwork or route.

As judged collector texture, the Hokushin'etsu print matters because Mew's mythic, hidden-specimen aura sits against mountain geography, making the card feel less like a stadium postcard and more like a regional secret.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu]: the secret in the mountains
narrative.why_it_matters: The Hokushin'etsu print has the best kind of quiet collector voltage. Mew is already the secret at the edge of early Pokémon memory, and here it is placed against the Japanese Alps rather than a grand city or monument. The result is a regional prize card that feels like a hidden route: tournament history, mountain geography, and one impossible little Pokémon tucked into the same Stadium.
not_claiming: resolution of every secondary-source date conflict

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, image, or agent claim says Lucky Stadium, Hokushin'etsu, Hokushinetsu, Mew, World Challenge Summer, Niigata, Japanese Alps, or May 14.
special_identification_instructions.summary: First establish the Hokushin'etsu/Mew/Summer route, then keep it separate from other regional Lucky Stadium prints and from later or bilingual Lucky Stadium releases.
steps: Check that the card is Lucky Stadium / ラッキースタジアム and that the claimed route is World Challenge Summer participation prize, not Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, Tropical Mega Battle, or Pokemon Center New York.

Confirm the regional identity is Hokushin'etsu / Hokushinetsu and the depicted Pokémon cue is Mew; do not substitute the other regional mascots such as Lugia, Ho-Oh, Pikachu, Zapdos, Onix, Gyarados, or Diglett.
Look for the Hokushin'etsu landmark cue: mountains of the Japanese Alps, and treat generic mountain language as insufficient unless tied back to this region.

Record Bulbapedia's July 26, 2000 Niigata City Industrial Promotion Center, Niigata listing as the current event-route anchor, while preserving PokeBoon's May 14, 2000 date as a visible secondary-source conflict rather than resolving it silently.
Treat source-page identity, artist credit, and release route as catalog legibility only; require seller photos, possession evidence, and card-condition evidence before a transaction gate.
not_claiming: that Mew or a mountain background alone proves the card is the Hokushin'etsu print

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 172 as Lucky Stadium, a Trainer/Stadium card from the World Challenge Summer participation-prize Hokushin'etsu conference slice, with Mew as the Pokémon cue.
Bulbapedia identifies the Hokushin'etsu World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium print as the Mew variant available at the Niigata City Industrial Promotion Center, Niigata on July 26, 2000.
PokeBoon identifies the card as Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushinetsu], unnumbered, and a World Challenge Summer participation prize.
Bulbapedia says the Hokushin'etsu print features several mountains of the Japanese Alps.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon both credit Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu] to "Big Mama" Tagawa and CR CG gangs.

As interpretive art context, the Tagawa/CR CG gangs credit places the Hokushin'etsu Mew print in the same early-CG apparatus that shaped Stadium cards, N64-era Pokémon modeling, and the odd Trainer-object visual language of the Neo era.

The Hokushin'etsu print should be separated from the other World Challenge Summer regional prints, the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, Pokemon Center New York, and generic Lucky Stadium listings because those carry different route, artwork, or language context.

As judged collector texture, Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu] is interesting because Mew turns a participation Stadium into something with secret-rare energy even though the source route is a regional attendance prize.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu]: secret-rare feeling, attendance-prize route
narrative.why_it_matters: Mew changes the temperature of the whole regional set. Hokushin'etsu is still a World Challenge Summer participation prize, but the character cue makes it feel like a hidden card even before money enters the room. That tension is the fun part: a public tournament object carrying the mood of Pokémon's earliest secret.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when evaluating a specific card image, listing, slab label, or seller claim for Lucky Stadium [Mew] [Hokushin'etsu].
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this card by the combined Hokushin'etsu + Mew + Japanese Alps + World Challenge Summer route, not by Lucky Stadium name or Mew appeal alone.
steps: Confirm the card name is Lucky Stadium / ラッキースタジアム and that the row is unnumbered promotional, not Neo Destiny 100/105 or another numbered print.
Confirm the variant claim says Hokushin'etsu / Hokushinetsu and shows Mew; if it shows a different Pokémon, route to the matching regional Lucky Stadium instead.
Check the artwork cue against the Japanese Alps mountain landmark; do not accept a generic mountain background or Mew label without source support.

If a source or listing uses May 14, 2000, preserve it as a secondary-source conflict unless supported by a stronger event archive; do not replace Bulbapedia's July 26, 2000 Niigata City Industrial Promotion Center anchor without evidence.
Before spending or trade gating, ask for seller-controlled photos and evidence of the actual card; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that a slab label alone resolves the variant
